title: Queued ≠ complete
lesson: A full queue can delay an agent tool submission; a free place admits the job, but admission is not successful tool completion.
limitations: Illustrative finite batch with one worker and three waiting places; job durations are not benchmarks.
FULL and SPACE visualize local admission feedback, not RabbitMQ protocol messages or acknowledgements.
Bounding waiting items does not guarantee bounded memory, request rate, deadlines, permissions, durability or exactly-once effects.
Audio was checked by waveform, spectrum, cue timing and encoded peak analysis; it was not physically listened to.
This is an author-reviewed alternative, not a comparative recommendation.

transcript.text: A documentation-check agent submits search job A. It passes through the queue, runs on the single tool worker, and completes normally.
Search job B runs slowly. C, D and E fill all three waiting places while B continues.
The full-queue signal pauses the agent with job F held outside the queue. F has not been admitted; existing tool work continues.
After B completes, removing C frees a place. The agent resumes and submits F. F is now queued, while C is running; admission has not completed F.
F stays queued while earlier search jobs finish. Only after D and E have run does F leave its waiting place for the tool worker.

F runs and its progress bar fills. Its state changes to complete only after execution finishes. The queue is empty and all six jobs have outcomes. This finite example is not a delivery or timing guarantee.
